newsitem.title: UK: Royal Sun says integration plans on target.
newsitem.headline: Royal Sun says integration plans on target.

text.p: British insurer Royal & Sun Alliance Group plc reported an 11 percent rise in first half profits on Thursday and said its integration plans remained on target to deliver the cost savings forecast for last year's merger.

Trading profits for the group, formed last year in a six billion pound ($9.6 billion) deal, rose to 501 million pounds despite the impact of recent sterling strength which took 25 million pounds off the headline figure.
The results marked the first year of Royal Sun's merged operation and the group said the integration process was still on course.
The company's top priority was to build shareholder value and it intended to deliver real dividend increases over time, said deputy chairman Roger Taylor.
Reflecting this, the half year dividend was raised 10 percent to 7.15 pence per share.
Taylor also reaffirmed the group's commitment to a more efficient capital structure and active management of its capital base.
General insurance profits rose 22 million pounds to 374 million pounds over the six months helped by an excellent performance in the U.S. and Canada, said chief executive Richard Gamble.
But in the UK profits slipped slightly to 165 million pounds from 172 million pounds last year.
Net asset value per share increased to 433 pence from 399 pence. As at August 4 it had risen to 455 pence. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
